3074.etyen:
Calque of English atomic bomb. Compound of atom (“atom”) + bombe (“bomb”), literally “atom bomb”.
The first element, atom (“atom”), is from Ancient Greek ἄτομος (átomos, “indivisible, uncut”), from ἀ- (a-, “not, without”) + τέμνω (témnō, “to cut”), the latter ultimately from the Proto-Indo-European root *temh₁- (“to cut”). The second element, bombe (“bomb”), is borrowed from French bombe (“bomb”), from Italian bomba (“bomb”), from Latin bombus (“booming or humming sound”), from Ancient Greek βόμβος (bómbos, “deep, hollow sound; humming, buzzing, booming”), an imitative formation.
Compare Norwe
